newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade at standstill -feedlots.

text.p: Trade in Plains feedlot cattle was at a standstill Thursday with showlists largely sold out, feedlot sources said.
"I think we're done for the week," a Kansas feedlot source said, noting packers were bidding $65.00 per cwt and asking for extra days.
"There ain't nobody going to do that," he said.
The bulk of trade this week has been at $66.00 per cwt.
Showlists for next week are expected to be slightly smaller than this week. For Kansas, it is seen around 5,000 head lower at about 90,000 with Texas off 2,000 head at 102,000 head.
"I think we have seen the hump (in the showlist)," one Kansas source said.
USDA reported, as of the close Wednesday, that week to date sales in Texas/west Oklahoma totalled 109,300 head and in Kansas 93,900 head.
Strong beef prices had aided the recent advance in cattle prices, with this week's trade up $2.00 from last week.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values for heavyweight choice were at the highest levels since December 1996 on Wednesday after rising $0.60 per cwt to $108.78.
